Recent Articles & Milestone Announcements

Archived articles capturing site ownership, medieval wall excavations, and volunteer community retrospectives.

press1 Oct 2025

Saving Grace Dieu Priory: An Appeal to the Local Community

Published in the Belton Maypole magazine: tracing 30 years from ivy-covered ruins in 1995 to public opening, and issuing a vital appeal for new volunteer blood.

Belton Maypole Magazine (October 2025 Edition)
discovery10 May 2025

800-Year-Old Medieval Priory Wall Uncovered by Volunteer Clearance

Clearing dense overgrowth and tidying paths with Charnwood Forest Geopark volunteers has revealed previously hidden sections of the 800-year-old Augustinian wall.

Friends of Grace Dieu Priory
announcement19 Feb 2025

Official Partnership with Charnwood Forest Geopark Announced

The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory are proud official partners of the Charnwood Forest Geopark as the region strives towards UNESCO Global Geopark designation.

Charnwood Forest Geopark
milestone15 Nov 2024

Grace Dieu Priory Sold to Charitable Trust: Permanent Ownership Secured

After two years of detailed negotiations with private landowners, the Grace Dieu Priory Trust has acquired the freehold ownership of the priory ruins and Rusty Mary's field.

BBC News

Grace Dieu Priory
Augustinian Canonesses · c. 1239

"Free to visit, cared for by volunteers for over 20 years."

Managed by The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory, a volunteer-run body dedicated to conserving the 13th-century ruins and keeping the site open to the public without statutory funding.

Visitor Code

Leave No TracePlease take all of your litter home with you. There are no public waste bins on the ancient monument ruins.
Dog WalkersDogs welcome on leads. A dedicated bin is located at the Bull's Head car park for dog litter bags (strictly none on-site).
Strict Site Policy: Paranormal events and ghost walks are expressly forbidden by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust across the entire priory site and surrounding lands.
